name: Rio Tinto Group

profile.description: Rio Tinto is a global diversified miner producing iron ore, copper, aluminium, lithium and other minerals, led since August 2025 by CEO Simon Trott under a 'stronger, sharper, simpler' strategy [3]. In H1 2026 underlying EBITDA rose 28% to $14.8B, copper EBITDA rose 84% to $5.7B, free cash flow rose 75%, and the interim ordinary dividend rose 43% to 211 US cents per share. The company also made first high-grade iron ore sales from Simandou in Guinea in April 2026 [1]. The ADR trades at $83.25, about $135.4B market cap [5].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Rio has shifted its earnings mix toward copper, where H1 2026 EBITDA rose 84% to $5.7B, and it brought Simandou, one of the world's largest high-grade iron ore projects, to first sales in April 2026 [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): Trott says Rio is concentrating digital and AI work on a select number of data-rich use cases such as geotechnical data and stepping up AI investment, but no quantified AI savings were found [3]. Market Share (1/2): Rio is a top-tier iron ore and copper producer, guiding 800-870 kt of 2026 consolidated copper, but in commodity markets where it is a price-taker [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Rio gives dated volume guidance: Simandou 2026 sales of 5-10 Mt (100% basis), copper of 800-870 kt, and 2026-27 capex of up to $11B [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FY2024 R&D of $398M was 0.7% of revenue, not top-quartile even by mining standards [6].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Rio's purpose, finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs, is clear, and the board's stated priority that 'everyone must go home safe, every day' is concrete [3]. However, its credibility was badly damaged when Rio destroyed the ancient Juukan Gorge rock shelters in 2020, which cost the CEO and two senior executives their jobs [4]. Community Impact (1/2): Rio runs large community and Indigenous-partnership programs as a condition of operating, but the Juukan Gorge fallout, including Ausbil dropping it from its sustainable fund, shows the gap between stated values and conduct [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and Trott is cutting key roles and rebuilding the executive team [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No director open-market buying data was found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically on Dividend-sleeve weights. D/E of 31.9% (1.0), ROE of 19.3% (1.0), revenue growth of 15.5% (1.0) and forward P/E of 9.8 (1.0) all hit target [5]. Profit margin of 19.6% scores 0.98 [5]. The 2020-2025 revenue CAGR of 5.3% ($44.6B to $57.8B) scores 0.69 [6]. Payout ratio of 54.5% scores 0.76 [5]. The ADR has paid a dividend every year since 1990, scoring 1.0 at 2x weight. Rio's variable payout policy means annual ADR dividends fell in 2023 ($4.02 vs $7.46) and 2025 ($3.73 vs $4.35), so consecutive years of growth is 0. The 5-year dividend CAGR is -0.7% ($3.86 in 2020 to $3.73 in 2025), scoring 0 at 2x weight [5]. Weighted sum of 8.43 out of 12 gives an Infrastructure score of 7 (7.02). Liquidity floor cleared: 2.26M average volume x $83.25 = about $189M per day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Rio digs physical ore out of the ground, and AI cannot substitute for iron ore, copper or aluminium. AI also raises demand for Rio's products: the board explicitly ties the strategy to copper demand from AI data centres, and copper is now Rio's fastest-growing earnings stream, with EBITDA up 84% in H1 2026 [1][3]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Rio benefits indirectly from AI-driven copper demand but discloses no revenue from AI products or services [3].

infinite_game.summary: Rio Tinto is making genuinely long-horizon bets in Simandou and Oyu Tolgoi. Sinek would judge, though, that its culture and leadership signals are those of a finite player: the Juukan Gorge destruction showed production targets overriding stated values, and CEO turnover has followed crises. The new 'every dollar must deliver value' cost-and-divestment program, and the ambition to be the 'most valued mining business', frame success in financial-ranking terms.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Rio's purpose of providing the materials the world needs, now framed around the energy transition and AI-driven copper demand, exists [3]. But Juukan Gorge showed it did not govern behaviour when it conflicted with production, and Trott's stated aim is to become the most valued mining business, a finite goal [3][4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Leadership has been repeatedly disrupted: the CEO and two senior executives were forced out over Juukan Gorge in 2020, and Trott replaced Stausholm in August 2025 and promptly cut key roles and rebuilt the executive team [3][4]. Productivity-driven restructuring with 80+ initiatives signals an organization under pressure rather than one built on psychological safety [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management frames its goal as becoming the 'most valued mining business', a ranking-against-peers mindset, and no evidence was found of leadership describing what rivals teach it [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Rio is steadily rebalancing from iron ore toward copper (H1 2026 copper EBITDA up 84%) and other transition minerals [1]. It remains a diversified miner, however, and the shift is a portfolio rotation rather than a reinvention of the business model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Rio committed multi-year capital to Simandou in Guinea and the Oyu Tolgoi underground in Mongolia despite political risk and cost overruns, and holds capex at up to $11B for 2026-27 [1][4]. These are genuine long-cycle bets, but they sit alongside a variable payout policy and a $5-10B cash-release program prioritizing near-term returns [1][3].

investment_thesis: Rio Tinto offers cheap exposure to copper and high-grade iron ore. H1 2026 underlying EBITDA rose 28% to $14.8B, free cash flow rose 75%, copper EBITDA rose 84% to $5.7B, and the interim dividend rose 43% to 211 cents per share at a 50% payout [1]. Simandou began high-grade sales in April with 5-10 Mt guided for 2026, and copper guidance of 800-870 kt is maintained [1]. At 9.8x forward earnings with D/E of 32%, ROE of 19% and a 5.6% yield [5], Rio is one of the cheapest large-cap ways to own AI- and electrification-driven copper demand.
thesis_continued: The bear case is commodity cyclicality and the reliability of the payout. Rio's variable dividend fell in 2023 and 2025, and the 5-year dividend CAGR is slightly negative (-0.7%) [5]. Iron ore still dominates earnings and is exposed to Chinese steel demand, which Simandou's added supply could depress. Simandou has shipped only 0.4 Mt so far against a 5-10 Mt target, so execution risk remains [1]. Trott's cost-cutting, divestment and leadership overhaul adds transition risk [3]. Juukan Gorge remains a reputational overhang with Indigenous communities and ESG investors [4].
key_catalysts: Simandou ramp-up toward the 5-10 Mt 2026 sales guidance (0.4 Mt shipped in H1) [1]
Copper production delivery against 800-870 kt 2026 guidance (442 kt in H1) as Oyu Tolgoi underground ramps up [1]
Execution of the up-to-$5B 2026 asset cash release and 80+ productivity initiatives under the 'stronger, sharper, simpler' plan [1][3]
key_risks: Iron ore price downturn driven by Chinese steel demand and new Simandou and Guinea supply [1]
Variable dividend policy: annual ADR dividends fell in 2023 and 2025, so income is not reliable [5]
Social-licence and sovereign risk in Guinea, Mongolia and Indigenous lands in Australia, where Juukan Gorge cost Rio its CEO [4]
